marta_sales: Quick heads up  ACME's security team approved a POC but insists on all traffic over Private connectivity (Direct Connect -> TGW). They asked whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is better for a short POC. Start window: next Wednesday. Who can provision endpoints + issue POC keys?

josh_solutions: I can run the provisioning. For a minimal-risk POC, Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) is simpler: no inbound ports, uses ENIs in their subnets, and we can lock an endpoint policy to only allow the POC API. Peering would require route table changes and possibly more firewall churn.

marta_sales: They want a note for the SOW about required network changes we can paste. Also asked about whether Hosted API keys can be used over PrivateLink or if we need Dedicated capacity.

priya_se: Short answer: Hosted API keys work over PrivateLink for POC traffic. If they need guaranteed throughput/SLA we'll recommend Dedicated (adds provisioning time and cost). For week 1 POC, Hosted + PrivateLink is fine. Confirm whether they need mTLSwe should ask.

tom_infra: Network checklist items from infra perspective: 1) Provide AWS account IDs and TGW attachment ID. 2) Subnets for VPCE ENIs (we need at least two AZs). 3) Ensure those subnets have free IPs for ENIs (each ENI consumes 1 IP). 4) Security group egress rule allowing outbound 443 to our service (we'll give exact ENI IPs after create). 5) DNS plan (Route53 resolver vs hosts override).

marta_sales: They provided accounts: 111122223333 (poc) and 444455556666 (prod). Suggested subnets: 10.30.5.0/24 and 10.30.6.0/24 in us-east-1. No mTLS for initial POC.

josh_solutions: Action plan I will execute: - Create Interface VPCE in us-east-1 with subnets 10.30.5.0/24 & 10.30.6.0/24. - Attach a restrictive endpoint policy scoped to the POC API. - Generate a short-lived Hosted API key bound to the POC project and share secure link. - Provide DNS + firewall guidance and a quick perf note.

josh_solutions: Quick CLI we will run from our infra account (using cross-account role into customer's account for VPCE creation):

`aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0aa11bb22cc --service-name com.amazonaws.us-east-1.execute-api --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-0aaa subnet-0bbb --security-group-ids sg-0abc --region us-east-1`

josh_solutions: Minimal endpoint policy we'll attach (we'll substitute exact API ARN):

`{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "execute-api:Invoke",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:execute-api:us-east-1:REDACTED:api-id/*/POST/*"
    }
  ]
}`

priya_se: DNS options reminder: (A) Route53 Private Hosted Zone + VPC association + Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint for on-prem DNS forwarding (recommended for anything beyond a day-long test). (B) For quick POC use: local hosts entries or internal DNS override mapping api.poc.redwood-inference.com -> vpce-*.us-east-1 IPs (manual but fastest).

tom_infra: Routing gotcha: If their on-premises appliance uses asymmetric NAT/DNAT you may see connection failures. Please ensure return path to the VPCE ENI IPs is via the TGW attachment. If they use a firewall performing SNAT, prefer SNAT to a NAT IP that is routable to our ENI IPs.

marta_sales: Cost note from buyer: will PrivateLink add extra egress charges? They want a 30-day estimate for ~200GB/month.

josh_solutions: Yes PrivateLink has AWS data processing fees plus cross-connect egress on their side. I'll produce a short estimate: PrivateLink processing + our normal egress *and* any DX/TGW transit fees on their side. I'll post numbers in the ticket.

infra-bot: CREATED TKT-4987: ACME POC privatelink provisioning  assignee: josh_solutions  due: 2026-05-02

marta_sales: Can you give me a cut-and-paste checklist for the SOW and the customer's network ops?

josh_solutions: Copyable SOW network checklist:
- Customer provides AWS account IDs and TGW attachment ID.
- Confirm VPCE subnets (two AZs): 10.30.5.0/24, 10.30.6.0/24.
- Ensure each subnet has at least 5 spare IPs for ENIs (we'll need 1 ENI per AZ).
- Add outbound allow rule: TCP 443 to the VPCE ENI IPs (we will provide exact CIDRs after creation).
- Choose DNS method: Route53 Resolver inbound (prod) or hosts override (POC).
- Verify on-prem return path to TGW: avoid asymmetric DNAT; if using NAT, configure SNAT to a routable IP.
- Customer to whitelist the issued API key ID and agree to rotate after POC.

marta_sales: Awesome, I'll paste that into the SOW and ask for the role ARNs for cross-account. Thanks all :tada:
